The 2019 detector (CCM120, 120 PMTs, about 5 t fiducial) was upgraded to CCM200 (200 PMTs, 7 t fiducial).

physics_goals.quote: CCM is a 10-ton liquid argon (LAr) detector located 20 meters from a high flux neutron/neutrino source and is designed to search for sterile neutrinos
physics_goals.value: Search for sterile neutrinos and light dark matter by coherent elastic scattering in 10 t of liquid argon, 20 m from the Lujan tungsten target

summary.plain: A 10-ton tank of liquid argon in the Lujan neutron-source building at Los Alamos, watched by light sensors, 20 metres from a tungsten target hit by protons. It looks for sterile neutrinos and for light dark matter that the proton beam might make.
summary.technical: Liquid-argon scintillation (and Cherenkov) light detector, 10 t of argon with a 7 t fiducial volume and 200 8-inch PMTs (CCM200; 120 PMTs in the 2019 CCM120 engineering run), 20 m from the Lujan tungsten target (800 MeV protons, 20 Hz, 290 ns spill). Searches for sterile neutrinos, leptophobic and other light dark matter, and axion-like particles via coherent elastic scattering and electromagnetic signals; first Cherenkov event-by-event identification from sub-MeV electrons in LAr.
